WHY IT MATTERS

Turn the feature into a better business process

An estimate sets expectations before work begins; conversion carries the agreed commercial details into billing and reduces avoidable re-entry.

01

Preserve agreed details

Customer information, item descriptions, quantities, prices, and terms remain easier to compare.

02

Reduce transcription mistakes

Reusing supported fields lowers the risk of typing a different amount or description on the invoice.

03

Keep approval and billing distinct

The estimate remains the pre-sale document while the converted draft becomes the payment request.

PRACTICAL CHECKLIST

Use estimates to invoices well

  • Record the validity period and assumptions on the estimate.
  • Confirm scope changes before creating the invoice.
  • Review every converted field before issuing the final document.
Always confirm the legal, tax, and record-keeping requirements that apply to your business.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions about estimates to invoices

Which documents can be converted?

The existing website describes conversion from estimates, sales orders, and proforma documents.

Does the original information carry over?

Supported customer, item, price, quantity, and term details can be reused in the invoice draft.

Can I edit the invoice afterward?

Yes. The result is described as an editable invoice draft that should be reviewed before completion.

What terminology does the workflow use?

Estimate is used consistently for the primary conversion workflow.
